NOMI

Every AI capability, in one place.

Coding agents, models and tools all live here, and Nomi is an agent too.

Watch them all, in one place.

Nomi's chats and background runs, the coding agents it dispatches and sessions you opened in a terminal or IDE all sit on the agent board with status, folder, memory and CPU; when memory runs low it pauses the coding agents Nomi dispatched and resumes them once it recovers.

Connect what you use.

Add a provider once and Nomi plus Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents can use any of its models, or run everything on local models.

Fully automatic, safely.

On macOS coding agents run in a system sandbox: they can't read your credentials and only write to the project folder; commands are risk-reviewed and data stays on your machine by default.

The agent workbench

Agent board

Filter by status and search; each card shows the agent, source, folder, CPU and memory, anything waiting on you comes first, and you can pause, resume or close it.

Workshop

Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and more in parallel; review the diff, commit or undo in a three-column workspace, with official accounts or any model.

Unified gateway

Four API protocols translated automatically: use DeepSeek, GLM or Kimi inside Claude Code, with retries and fallback built in; third-party providers can be added from a web link in one click.

Tasks & background work

Tell Nomi once and it keeps track, running on a schedule or on web, GitHub and folder events; long jobs like an image set or a deck go to a background Nomi, coding goes to coding agents in an isolated worktree, and you can follow or stop everything on the tasks page.

Optional: Nomi on your desktop

Want some company? Keep Nomi on your desktop: it gives a thumbs-up when a task finishes and apologizes when one fails, summarizes files you drop on it, and talks with you by voice. Don't need it? Close it from its toolbar; the workbench works the same.

About the desktop character

Local first. You set the boundaries.

Conversations, memory and knowledge are stored on your computer by default. You decide which external services to connect, API keys and other secrets are protected before they leave, and you can let only local models read your files.
